_about: Host wall-clock timing for the 2-D ladder engine, reported by the operator on 2026-11-12 and banked here verbatim. This is a NEW record; artifacts/ladder_engine_scaling.json is untouched and remains the container-side 7-run record. Nothing in this file was measured inside this repository or this container.
notes: host measured; container is 2.15x slower for cpp

provenance.manner: hand-copied from the operator's report; not regenerated by any script in this repository
provenance.withheld_experiment: no script here produced these numbers, so they cannot be re-derived, only re-read

thread_count.basis: emfit/_env.py pin_threads (lines 44-70) sets OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 when unset, and emfit/__init__.py calls it at lines 33-37. If the timed runs imported the package they ran one thread. This is an inference from that code path, not a measurement: no artefact in this repository records a thread count, and artifacts/ladder_engine_scaling.json says so itself - each of its seven runs carries a threads block with recorded_in_artefact false and artefact_keys_matching_thread_or_omp set to the empty list, which is the search the artefact's own field_sources.threads string reports as returning [] in all seven.

mesh_cells.basis: artifacts/ladder_engine_scaling.json records structure C at geometry.cells = 289168 with 2400 steps and a 0.4 mm cell, so the mesh this timing refers to is the committed one.

python_runs_internal_consistency.basis: ARITHMETIC: the five python runs mean 49.62 (reported 49.6); their sample standard deviation is 9.22 (reported 9.0); spread is 18.6% of the mean. The reported summary statistics match the reported runs to within rounding, so the run list and the mean/std are one consistent record, not a transcription of two unrelated columns.

corrections.status: ARITHMETIC MISMATCH - 2.15 does not follow from any pair of the published container figures

recomputed.comparison: unpinned container cpp vs host cpp
OMP-pinned-1 container cpp vs host cpp

corrections.why_two_arms: artifacts/ladder_engine_scaling.json carries two container cpp arms for the same structure, 58.04 s unpinned and 43.20 s with OMP_NUM_THREADS pinned to 1. They are 1.34x apart, so the container side of this comparison is only resolved to roughly +/-34%. Both arms are stated rather than one of them picked silently.
corrections.standing_consequence: The container-vs-host cpp penalty is therefore somewhere between 1.57x and 2.12x on the published numbers. Nobody should quote a single figure for it until the same thread pinning is applied to both sides.

corrections.claim: (implied by the note) the container slows the engine down generally
corrections.reading: Python runs within 1% of the host figure inside the container, so the container penalty described above is specific to the cpp engine and is most likely a threading/environment effect rather than general container slowness.

container_comparators_from: artifacts/ladder_engine_scaling.json (committed, blob 27146d7): structure C, wall_total, cpp 58.04084487300133 unpinned, cpp 43.200629351020325 with OMP pinned to 1, python 50.11570404301165
verdict: These numbers are OPERATOR-REPORTED. They are internally consistent and consistent with the committed mesh, but nothing in this repository produced or re-derived them, and no thread count was recorded. Treat as evidence of what the operator measured, not as a reproduced result.
